question: A 10-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain. Four days ago, she visited a petting zoo with her family. Her temperature is 39.4°C (102.9°F). Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation of the right lower quadrant. Stool cultures at 42°C grow colonies that turn black after adding phenylenediamine. Which of the following best describes the most likely causal organism?

options.opa: Gram-negative, non-flagellated bacteria that do not ferment lactose
options.opb: Gram-positive, anaerobic, rod-shaped bacteria that form spores
options.opc: Gram-negative, flagellated bacteria that do not ferment lactose
options.opd: Gram-positive, aerobic, rod-shaped bacteria that produce catalase
options.ope:
Gram-positive, aerobic, rod-shaped bacteria that form spores
"

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Exposure to petting zoo -> Ingestion of contaminated food or water -> Development of gastrointestinal symptoms -> 70% CHAIN: Bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain -> Suspected infectious etiology -> Stool cultures performed -> 80% CHAIN: Growth of colonies that turn black after adding phenylenediamine -> Likely presence of Salmonella species -> 90% CHAIN: Salmonella species -> Gram-negative, non-flagellated bacteria that do not ferment lactose -> 70%
enhanced_information: The most likely causal organism in this case is a Gram-negative, non-flagellated bacteria that do not ferment lactose, consistent with the likely presence of Salmonella species based on the growth of colonies that turn black after adding phenylenediamine in the stool cultures.
analysis: The core medical principle here is to identify the likely causal organism based on the clinical presentation and laboratory findings. The presence of bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and the growth of colonies that turn black after adding phenylenediamine in stool cultures suggest a Gram-negative, non-flagellated bacteria that does not ferment lactose. Salmonella species are known to fit this description and are commonly associated with petting zoos. This aligns with the enhanced information provided.
